podcast.body: Featured on his 1999 album "Brand New Day," this song was a collaboration with Algerian singer Cheb Mami, showcasing Mami's vocals in Arabic alongside Sting's mix of English and Arabic lyrics, set against electronic production. Co-written by Sting to highlight Mami's voice, it took months to catch on. Car maker Jaguar licensed it for commercials, which spurred American radio play. It debuted on the Hot 100 in May 2000, becoming a sleeper hit, spending 26 weeks on the chart and rising to number 17. "Sting had grown enamored of Mami's voice and co-wrote Desert Rose specifically to showcase Mami's vocals alongside Sting's own."
